title: Thresholded operator cohort for gradual autosuggest activation
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Summary: Implement an operator-cohort based gated rollout that automatically applies Optimize batching/caching recommendations only after passing telemetry thresholds and explicit operator cohort acknowledgement. This work builds a thresholded, auditable path between the Optimize suggestions engine and the config applier so teams can safely realize cost savings without risking regressions to latency, accuracy, or downstream failures.

Background: Optimize currently generates per-route batching/cache recommendations. Previous manual adoption is slow; earlier attempts at full auto-apply raised operational incidents and unwanted regressions. We need a middle ground: automated activation for low-risk recommendations with human-in-the-loop for higher-risk changes.

Goals:
- Define an "operator cohort" (small set of oncall/ops users) who receive proposed autoactivations and can approve/rollback quickly.
- Enforce telemetry thresholds (latency, 95/99 p50/p95/p99 token times, error rate, quality regressions) before and after canary windows.
- Implement a staged activation mesh: shadow -> partial canary -> cohort approval -> broad rollout.
- Provide observability dashboard and time-bound approval windows (escrow) with automatic safe rollback.

Non-goals:
- This does not change model-level routing or model architecture selection.
- Does not introduce new quantization profiles in this sprint.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Undetected quality regressions. Mitigation: require evaluation on golden prompt set and monitor false-positive/negative deltas; fail activation on negative signal.
- Risk: Approval latency causes missed cost savings. Mitigation: allow pre-approved low-risk classes with stricter telemetry gates.
- Risk: Cohort approvers become single point of failure. Mitigation: escalate to secondary cohort and automatic conservative fallback if approval not received in escrow window.

High-level approach:
1) Suggestion metadata: extend Optimize suggestion payload with risk_score, signature (fingerprint), and a recommended canary_config object.
2) Canonical canary mesh controller: service that orchestrates shadowing, injecting canary traffic (percent, routes), and evaluating telemetry windows.
3) Operator cohort flow: slack/email + Console modal where cohort members see diff, telemetry projections, playbook, and can approve/deny. Approvals recorded with user id and timestamp.
4) Escrowed auto-commit: if cohort approves or suggestion is low risk and telemetry gates pass, commit via config applier; else rollback or hold.

Data & telemetry gates (initial set):
- Latency p95 delta <= 10% or +50ms absolute
- Error rate delta <= 0.2% absolute
- Token throughput drop <= 5% for commit window
- Quality regression: evaluation BLEU/QA-metric delta <= 0.5% absolute; for chat models use downstream prompt acceptance rate on held set
- Health checks: any increase in internal 5xxs or gateway timeouts fails the gate

Acceptance criteria (must all be true):
acceptance_criteria: Canary mesh controller can execute a shadow run for a suggestion and collect telemetry for the configured window
Operator cohort UI shows pending activations with diffs, expected cost savings, and projected telemetry impacts
Escrow approvals recorded and visible in audit log (user id, time, comment)
Automated commit only occurs when telemetry gates are satisfied and cohort approval exists (or low-risk auto-approval policy applies)
Automatic rollback triggers if post-commit telemetry crosses rollback thresholds within the defined rollback window
End-to-end e2e tests for the controller and applier exist and run in CI with simulated traffic
tasks: Design: finalize canary window durations and gate thresholds (ops + SRE + research)
API: add risk_score and canary_config to Optimize suggestion payload (backend)
Controller: implement canary mesh orchestration service with traffic partitioning hooks
Console: cohort approval UI modal + audit view + escalation options
Telemetry: ensure metric slices (route/model/tenant) are available and exposed to controller
Playbook: write incident rollback runbook and add to Console help
QA: create simulator harness for canary runs and negative testcases
Docs: update Optimize docs and runbook
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Decided to start with per-route canaries rather than global because risk surface is smaller and rollback impact is limited
2025-02-18: Agreed to treat suggestions with risk_score<=0.15 as eligible for auto-approval if telemetry gates pass
2025-02-24: Chose 30m canonical canary window for first pass; shorter 10m warmup followed by 20m evaluation
2025-02-28: Require at least two distinct operator approvals for high-impact (>20% cost delta) activations
notes: Implementation will reuse traffic partitioning primitives from the serving runtime; ENG infra already exposed an API (see ENG-572490)
Security review requested because applier will write route config (KMS keys required for auditing)
We should avoid creating a new user role; leverage existing ops role and add a 'cohort_approver' flag

2025-02-20 - Priya Nair (SRE): Added suggested gate thresholds and recommended making cost delta a multi-tier signal (safety threshold vs business threshold).
2025-02-25 - Design review: PM requested that the Console modal include a one-click 'simulate activation' that runs the suggestion through the controller in dry-run mode.
